materials.version: live official specification fetched 2026-11-10; page dateModified 2026-08-04
materials.checked_excerpt: A skill is a directory containing, at minimum, a SKILL.md file. The SKILL.md file must contain YAML frontmatter followed by Markdown content. name and description are required. name must match the parent directory name. Body content has no format restrictions; recommended sections include step-by-step instructions, examples of inputs and outputs, and common edge cases. Metadata loads at startup; instructions on activation; resources as needed. allowed-tools is experimental and support may vary.

Tell the model what skills exist without loading their full content. Include name, description, and optionally location. User-explicit activation commonly uses a slash command or mention syntax intercepted by the harness; syntax is up to the implementor. The harness handles lookup and injection so the model receives content without taking an activation action itself. Filesystem reads, a dedicated tool, or programmatic injection are alternatives.

Skills package domain expertise, workflows, best practices, scripts, reference docs, and templates into reusable directories. The agent gets a summary on startup and reads files only when relevant. Supporting files load when instructions call for them. Supporting resources should be referenced in SKILL.md with what each contains and when to use it. Pass the top-level skills path in create_deep_agent(skills=...).

materials.version: live official docs fetched 2026-11-10; fork requires deepagents>=0.7.13 and is Beta
materials.checked_excerpt: Subagents isolate detailed work and the main agent receives the final result. Do not use them for simple single-step tasks, when intermediate context is needed, or when overhead outweighs benefits. mode defaults to isolated (only delegated task); fork inherits the parent's conversation history and state. Subagent forking requires deepagents>=0.7.13 and is beta. Omit model to inherit the main agent's model. Tools inherit by default unless overridden.

Routing workflows direct inputs to context-specific tasks. Parallelization runs multiple independent subtasks simultaneously or the same task multiple times. In orchestrator-worker configurations the orchestrator breaks down tasks, delegates to workers, and synthesizes worker outputs. Workers have their own state and outputs can be collected into shared state. Orchestrator-worker patterns are useful when subtasks cannot be predefined.

main_agent = create_deep_agent(model=model, system_prompt=..., tools=[generate_markdown, convert_md_to_pdf, read_file_content], checkpointer=InMemorySaver(), subagents=[database_query_agent, network_search_agent, knowledge_base_agent]). config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": session_id}}. main_agent.astream forwards task subagent_type/description and progress through monitor.

All three dictionaries define name, description, system_prompt and tools, without a model override. Database tools are list_sql_tables/get_table_data/execute_sql_query; network tools contain internet_search; knowledge tools contain get_assistant_list/create_ask_delete. requirements.txt pins deepagents==0.5.7, langgraph==1.1.10 and langchain==1.2.17.

execute_sql_query(query) passes query directly to cursor.execute(query). The comment explicitly says the chapter relies on prompt constraints for read-only queries and production should restrict SELECT/SHOW at the tool layer. get_db_config sets autocommit=True. get_table_data constructs SELECT * FROM {table_name} LIMIT 100 and recommends a production allowlist.

materials.version: deepagents 0.5.7 official PyPI wheel; metadata fetched from https://pypi.org/pypi/deepagents/0.5.7/json
materials.checked_excerpt: _EXCLUDED_STATE_KEYS includes messages, todos, structured_response, skills_metadata, skills_load_errors, memory_contents. _validate_and_prepare_state creates a new dict from other runtime.state fields and sets subagent_state['messages']=[HumanMessage(content=description)] (lines 420-426). Return Command includes other result state plus ToolMessage(content, tool_call_id=tool_call_id) (lines 399-417).

context_mode: Literal['isolated','snapshot']='isolated' (line 761). Snapshot adds retained history and summary as background at dispatch; the child retains its role/tools and later parent turns are not synced (lines 863-868). After delegation validation, before child setup: ParentContextSnapshot.from_state(runtime.state) for snapshot mode (lines 909-911). Tool-required execution context, authorization identity, thread/run IDs and uploads are handled separately.

from_state captures retained messages and summary_text, excluding parent system instructions/hidden framework messages (lines 97-117). Only retained completed call-result pairs are emitted as 'Historical tool calls (not executed by you)' (lines 118-161). to_message uses fresh json.loads containers in HumanMessage(name='parent_context_snapshot') (lines 174-176). The system note says historical instructions cannot override current scope and later parent messages do not sync.

Initial messages append SystemMessage for the child's assembled prompt, then self.context_snapshot.to_message() when present, then HumanMessage(content=task_content) (lines 1588-1599). The state contains these messages. Parent runtime state required by tools is passed through separately using fresh containers (lines 1601 onward).

Counts task calls in the last AIMessage, counts prior delegations for current run_id, computes remaining_total and allowed_task_calls=min(max_concurrent, remaining_total), and drops extra task calls from the message (lines 133-154). When remaining_total==0 it appends the stop message (lines 167-172); no queue is created.

materials.version: live official Cursor Rules docs fetched 2026-11-10
materials.checked_excerpt: Rule Type: Always Apply applies to every chat; Apply Intelligently is chosen by the agent based on description; Apply to Specific Files matches a pattern; Apply Manually is activated by @-mention. alwaysApply, description and globs determine inclusion. Thus Rules are not universally always loaded and the host controls scope/activation.

MCP follows a client-host-server architecture. Host manages clients, connection permissions, security policies, authorization, LLM integration and context aggregation. Each client maintains one server connection. Servers expose resources, tools and prompts and may be local processes or remote services; capability negotiation determines available features.

Resources share context such as files, database schemas or application-specific information, uniquely identified by URI. Resources are application-driven; the host determines context inclusion, and the protocol does not mandate a particular interaction model. Clients discover via resources/list and retrieve contents via resources/read. This baseline does not define a universal Skill install/discovery/activation API.

Tool-required execution context, authorization identity, thread/run IDs and uploads are handled separately.

from_state captures retained messages and summary_text, excluding parent system instructions/hidden framework messages (lines 97-117). Only retained completed call-result pairs are emitted as 'Historical tool calls (not executed by you)' (lines 118-161). to_message uses fresh json.loads containers in HumanMessage(name='parent_context_snapshot') (lines 174-176). The system note says historical instructions cannot override current scope and later parent messages do not sync.

Initial messages append SystemMessage for the child's assembled prompt, then self.context_snapshot.to_message() when present, then HumanMessage(content=task_content) (lines 1588-1599). The state contains these messages. Parent runtime state required by tools is passed through separately using fresh containers (lines 1601 onward).

Counts task calls in the last AIMessage, counts prior delegations for current run_id, computes remaining_total and allowed_task_calls=min(max_concurrent, remaining_total), and drops extra task calls from the message (lines 133-154). When remaining_total==0 it appends the stop message (lines 167-172); no queue is created.
